question.problem: Suppose that $y$ varies inversely with $x$ and that $y=\frac{3}{4}$ when $x=12.$ Then, if $x=\frac{1}{3},$ $y=${{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
Since $y$ varies inversely with $x,$ we use the equation

$$
y=\frac{k}{x}.
$$

We are told that $y=\frac{3}{4}$ when $x=12.$ We substitute this data into the equation to find $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4} & =\frac{k}{12} \\ \frac{3}{4}\cdot 12 & =k \\ 9 & =k\end{aligned}
$$

So, the inverse variation is given by 

$$
y=\frac{9}{x}.
$$

Finally, substituting the value of $x=\frac{1}{3}$ into this equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{9}{(\frac{1}{3})} \\  & =9÷(\frac{1}{3}) \\  & =9\cdot (\frac{3}{1}) \\  & =27.\end{aligned}
$$
